fieldMarks: Legless with movable eyelids, external ear openings, a lateral fold and a tail up to three-quarters of total length; 38-66 cm.
Dark middorsal stripe (sometimes faint) bordered by tan and another dark stripe; 3-4 narrow dark stripes above the lateral fold continuing onto the tail.
Below the lateral fold, marking is reduced to freckles, spots or dashes; 95 or fewer scales along the lateral fold.
Smallest of the four Florida glass lizards; lateral striping poorly developed in juveniles.
behavior: Surface records run 27 March to 16 November, peaking April-June; less active in winter, possibly underground.
Forages actively by day in open habitat and shelters under boards and debris; tail breaks off when seized.
habitat: Longleaf (occasionally slash) pine uplands with grassy groundcover, especially mesic to wet flatwoods; occasionally hillside seepage bogs, dome swamp edges and wet prairies next to pine uplands.
range: Coastal Plain of the southeastern United States, including Florida, coastal South Carolina and coastal and southern Georgia; rare and poorly documented. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Snakes (legless look-alikes)
lookalikes.howToTell: Snakes have wide belly scales, fixed eye coverings, no ear openings, short tails and more flexible bodies.

lookalikes.name: Slender glass lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Mimic has a low lateral-fold scale count (95 or fewer); the species are separated by colour pattern and scalation.
